title: HelixNode Systems - Channel & Sprint Planning Intro
summary: Introductory discovery between Redwood and HelixNode to explore channel reseller partnership and technical integration patterns. High-level alignment on go-to-market model (reseller + co-sell), pilot scoping for a 6-week proof-of-concept focused on low-latency LLM inference for HelixNode customers, and technical constraints (VPC/private control plane, SOC2, KMS). SE agreed to share an integration playbook, initial sizing and benchmark plan. Customer wants a sprint cadence and clear success metrics before committing to a pilot.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-02-28
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Rita Kumar (HelixNode Head Partnerships), Samir Patel (CTO), Leah Ong (Infra Lead), Marcus Li (Partnerships Ops)

[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Avery, AE on this account at Redwood. Diego's with me, he'll cover the technical bits. How are we all doing?
[00:10] Rita Kumar: Good, thanks. Busy week but excited to chat through this.
[00:15] Samir Patel: Yep, hello from NYC. We wanted to run through how a channel partnership might work and what the integration lift looks like.
[00:25] Diego Morales: Great — quick agenda: market motion (reseller/co-sell), deployment models (hosted, dedicated, private/VPC), initial pilot scope, and a rough sprint plan. Sound OK?
[00:35] Marcus Li: Sounds good. We're mostly exploring resell + integrated offering with HelixNode control plane.
[01:05] Rita Kumar: For context — HelixNode sells an edge orchestration product to telco customers. We want to add inference as a managed option. We don't want to become inference operators. So we need a partner that can integrate into our billing and reseller flows.
[01:20] Avery Chen: Understood. Typical pattern we see is Redwood acts as the inference provider: we offer hosted API for quick time-to-value, Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput tied to reserved commits, then Private/VPC if customers need full network isolation. For partners you can resell hosted or broker dedicated instances for customers. We have a partner playbook that outlines margins and technical obligations.
[02:02] Samir Patel: Quick Q — how does billing integration work? We want to consolidate into one invoice for the customer and keep some margin.
[02:10] Avery Chen: Two common flows: 1) you resell and we invoice HelixNode via a partner contract, or 2) Redwood invoices the end-customer and shares revenue via partner settlement. We can provide an example reseller agreement and invoicing API.
[02:35] Leah Ong: From infra perspective, customers will insist on VPC/private deployments for certain telco customers. Is that a separate product? How much lift is that?
[02:50] Diego Morales: Private is essentially a customer-specific control plane with a data plane that can be run in your VPC or on-prem. There's an initial integration: networking (VPN/DirectConnect), IAM/KMS integrations, and an on-prem package for air-gapped. Usually SE-led work for first deployment, then we hand over runbooks. It does take more time than hosted, typically 4-8 weeks depending on approvals.
[03:30] Marcus Li: And SOC2? We need to make sure we can present SOC2 and ISO artifacts for our customers.
[03:40] Avery Chen: We are SOC 2 Type II, have ISO docs, and can provide audit logs and configurable retention. For partner offerings we can also surface per-customer audit logs. I'll attach our security pack.
[04:05] Rita Kumar: Great. On the technical side, latency is a big deal for our use-case. We need 50-80ms p95 for short chat prompts and under 200ms for longer eval flows. How do you support that across regions and for edge customers?
[04:25] Diego Morales: We route requests by policy; we have region-aware routing, model variants optimized for latency, and dedicated pools to guarantee tail latencies. For telco edge customers we typically recommend Dedicated capacity or Private with pinned GPUs close to the edge. We'll need to size GPUs and consider quantization. We also have prefix/KV caching to lower token cost and latency for repeat prompts.
[05:10] Samir Patel: What's the typical hardware mix and cost for that latency? We need a ballpark before committing to pilot.
[05:20] Diego Morales: Ballpark depends on model and concurrency. For a heavy Llama-family 70B-ish workload we typically use an A100/ H100 mix, or cheaper nodes with quantization for cost tradeoffs. We'll send a sizing spreadsheet. For pilot you can start with a smaller pool and simulate traffic.
[06:00] Rita Kumar: On the integration side, we have a preference that the control plane is co-managed. We need to embed some UI hooks in HelixNode console so customers can enable inference, see usage, and provision. Is that feasible?
[06:12] Avery Chen: Yes — we have APIs for provisioning, tokens, and a usage API. Partners often build a lightweight UI integration and call our APIs. We also expose webhooks for billing events and model events.
[06:40] Leah Ong: Security — KMS integration is a hard requirement. Can we bring our own KMS and HSM?
[06:50] Diego Morales: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated. For hosted we can integrate with partner KMS via a vetted path, but the cleanest model is Private with your KMS. We'll need an implementation plan for key wrapping and credential rotation.
[07:30] Marcus Li: How do you handle failure/fallbacks? If a Dedicated pool goes down, do you have automatic fallback to hosted?
[07:40] Diego Morales: We support smart routing and fallback policies — yes, you can configure automatic fallback to compatible hosted model variants. There's also canary/rollout tooling for model updates so you minimize regressions.
[08:10] Rita Kumar: Ok good. Let's talk pilot scope. We're thinking 6-week pilot with 3 HelixNode end-customers: one enterprise telco, one mid-market streaming partner, and one internal demo. Success metrics: p95 latency under 150ms for critical flows, <20% cost delta vs their current model, and integration of provisioning in HelixNode console. Thoughts?
[08:40] Avery Chen: That sounds achievable. We'll propose a 6-week plan: week 0-1 on onboarding and network (VPC setup), week 2-3 deploy and run benchmarks, week 4-5 test with real traffic, week 6 finalize runbook and handoff. Diego will produce the test/benchmark plan and sizing.
[09:10] Samir Patel: How do you prevent model quality regression if we swap quantized models? We can't drop output quality for customers.
[09:22] Diego Morales: We have evaluation harnesses and quality gating. For quantized model variants we run prompt sets and have regression alerts. If quality drops we can route to a higher-fidelity model automatically. We'll include evaluation thresholds in the pilot plan.
[10:05] Leah Ong: Are there network port requirements? We need a list for our security team.
[10:12] Diego Morales: Yes — we'll share a concise network checklist (eg, ports, allowed IPs, cert requirements).
[10:30] Rita Kumar: From go-to-market, we want co-marketing and a joint case study post-pilot. Also partner enablement docs so our sales org can sell the add-on.
[10:42] Avery Chen: Absolutely — partner enablement kit, one-pager, and a joint webinar can be part of the package. We'll include sample co-marketing assets.
[11:15] Marcus Li: Competitors question — some of our customers are asking why choose Redwood vs VeloxCompute; what differentiators should we emphasize?
[11:25] Avery Chen: Emphasize production-first runtime (predictable latency and cost controls), unified APIs across hosted/dedicated/private, and developer-friendly SDKs. Also highlight our quantization recommendations and rollout tooling.
[12:05] Samir Patel: Ok logistics — can we run an initial PoC using hosted while the VPC work is being approved? We need something quick.
[12:12] Diego Morales: Yes, hosted is fastest. We can provision test keys and a sandbox model catalog within days. That will let you iterate on console integration and basic benchmarks while VPC approvals are in flight.
[13:00] Rita Kumar: Good. Can you send a sample contract and pricing ballpark for dedicated pools and per-token hosted?
[13:06] Avery Chen: Yes, I'll send pricing ranges and the reseller template. Diego will attach the sizing sheet.
[13:30] Leah Ong: One more infra question — how do you handle KV/prefix cache if calls are routed across regions? State consistency is a concern.
[13:45] Diego Morales: Good question. We do locality-aware caching; for multi-region customers we either shard caches per-region or use a central store with acceptable tradeoffs. We'll include architecture options in the playbook.
[14:20] Rita Kumar: Great — I think that's enough for now. Let's lock on the immediate next steps and owners.
[14:30] Avery Chen: Recap: we'll send partner playbook + security pack + sample contract. Diego will share sizing sheet + benchmark plan + network checklist. HelixNode to share three prioritized pilot customers and any existing SLAs. We'll schedule a deep-dive with Leah's infra team the week of March 6.
[14:55] Samir Patel: Works for us. Thanks everyone.
[15:00] Avery Chen: Thanks all — we'll follow up in email with artifacts and a calendar invite for the infra deep dive.

Notes about transcript: occasional auto-transcription errors — product names sometimes appear as Redwood Dedic8 or Redwood Dedication; KV cache sometimes transcribed as K-V cash or key-value cash. Some crosstalk around 08:00-09:00 during pilot planning.
